messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). If you’re comfortable, tune it to standard tuning (E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E). | A well‑presented instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the whole instrument from multiple angles (front, back, sides, headstock, bridge, strings). Include close‑ups of any scratches, dents, or repairs. | Good photos reduce buyer hesitation and can justify a higher asking price. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds. Look at similar models, ages, and conditions. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively without underselling. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | • **Title**: “Acoustic Guitar – [Brand] [Model] – [Year] – Excellent Condition”
• **Description**: Mention brand, model, year, wood type, any upgrades, condition notes, and why you’re selling.
• **Price**: Set a firm price or “Negotiable” if you’re flexible. | A concise, honest description builds trust and attracts serious buyers. | | **5. Choose Your Platforms** | • **Reverb** – Great for musical instruments; offers buyer protection.
• **eBay** – Wide audience; auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist/Facebook Marketplace** – Local sales, no shipping hassles.
• **Local Music Stores** – Some buy used gear or offer consignment.
• **Pawn Shops** – Quick cash, but usually lower offers. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Local Pickup**: Faster, no shipping cost, safer for both parties.
• **Shipping**: Use a sturdy case or padded box, insure the package, and ship via tracked service. | Shipping adds cost and risk; local pickup is often preferred for instruments. | | **7. Set Payment Terms** | • **Cash**: Safe for local sales.
• **PayPal**: Offers buyer/seller protection.
• **Bank Transfer**: Secure but verify before shipping.
• **Escrow**: For high‑value items. | Clear payment terms prevent disputes and protect against fraud. | | **8. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | • Respond promptly.
• Keep tone friendly but firm.
• Be prepared to explain your price and any repairs. | Good communication can turn a hesitant buyer into a sale. | | **9. Finalize the Sale** | • Sign a simple bill of sale (especially for high‑value items).
• Provide any original paperwork (manuals, receipts). | Documentation protects both parties and can be useful for future resale. | | **10. Follow Up** | • Ask for a quick review or feedback.
• Keep the listing active until sold. | Positive reviews boost credibility for future listings. | ### Quick Tips - **Timing**: List during the spring or early summer when people are more likely to buy instruments for new projects or lessons. - **Safety**: Meet in a public place or have a friend present if you’re meeting strangers. - **Avoid Scams**: Never accept money before handing over the instrument. Verify the buyer’s identity if possible. ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2010 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2010 - Wood: Spruce top, mahogany back & sides - Condition: Minor scuff on the back, no cracks, fully functional - Extras: Original case, extra strings, cleaning kit - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string Price: $350 (Negotiable) Photos: [Attach 5–6 high‑resolution images] Payment: PayPal or cash (local pickup preferred) ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your specific guitar. Good luck with your sale!
